feedback: D1 catalogues all ten slots and the OWASP classes and CWEs are mostly right (CWE-89 SQLi, CWE-347 alg:none, CWE-798 hardcoded secret, CWE-613 missing expiry, CWE-79 XSS, CWE-611 XXE, CWE-22 traversal, CWE-601 redirect), so the class work is solid and I credited the MD5 entry even though you used CWE-328 rather than CWE-916. What pulls this row down is that no finding carries a quoted source line or a capture timestamp, you never name the actual hardcoded secret sankofa-legacy-admin-2019, and the cookie missing Secure and SameSite finding (CWE-614) is absent, replaced by an F10 Customer PII Exposure entry that is really an impact, not a tenth vulnerability. The decoy is wrong: the safe construct in this pack is the HS256 verify branch that uses hash_equals(), which is constant-time and sound, so the real bugs are alg:none and the hardcoded secret. You named JWT role manipulation on Token 3 as the false positive and proved nothing at the mechanism level, so that six-point row earned nothing in D1 and again in D3. D2 has the chain in the right order and includes genuine verbatim payloads (the OR 1=1 login, the cookie-beacon script, the path traversal request, the XXE entity), which is the strongest part of this deliverable, but only Hop 1 is reconciled to a real capture line (02:14:08) and the rest have no timestamps, so the reconciliation that the key asks for is mostly missing. Your SQLi CVSS is 9.8 with A:H, which is wrong: the auth bypass does not affect availability, so the vector should be CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N at about 9.1, and you also missed the senior insight that a forged super_admin token reaches the shared /api/v1/internal service, which is a real scope change to S:C. The naira impact stayed at several million with no per-customer math, where the export shows balances up to about 950k summing to tens of millions across 312 customers tied to the BoltCash launch in roughly six weeks, so state those assumptions and do the arithmetic. D3 reads cleanly and the executive summary is jargon-free and lands on 312 customers and the data types, but it has no naira headline and very little explicit threat model, and you state outright that you ordered remediation by impact severity rather than effort, which caps that row at half because the key wants effort-to-risk ordering. Your two detection stopgaps name useful patterns but give qualitative false-positive labels (Low, Very Low) rather than an exact field and a numeric FP rate. D4 is the best deliverable: you answer all four prompts in your own voice, cite ISC2 Canon I by number in a load-bearing way, name NDPA 2023 Section 40 tied to the 312 affected customers, and anchor your stance to the actual investigation artifacts. I looked hard for a way to push this into the 60s and the class accuracy and the real payloads got partial credit, but the absence of any quoted source lines in D1, the wrong decoy repeated across D1 and D3, the A:H SQLi vector, and remediation by severity instead of effort genuinely hold it at this mark. The single most important fix: identify and prove the real decoy, the constant-time hash_equals() HS256 branch, instead of guessing at JWT role manipulation, and back every finding with a quoted line and its capture timestamp.
